conclusions: The Lebesgue lower integral over t in (0, infinity) of the standard Cauchy upper-tail mass P(X > t) equals infinity.
The Lebesgue lower integral over t in (-infinity, 0) of the standard Cauchy lower-tail mass P(X < t) equals infinity.
mathematical_definitions: Let X have the Cauchy probability measure with location 0 and scale 1.
For t > 0, the first integrand is the Cauchy measure of {x in Real | t < x}.
For t < 0, the second integrand is the Cauchy measure of {x in Real | x < t}.
Both integrals are ENNReal-valued lower integrals with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to the indicated open half-line.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For a standard Cauchy random variable, both the integral of its upper-tail probability over positive thresholds and the integral of its lower-tail probability over negative thresholds diverge to positive infinity.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition is closed: it has no binders or hypotheses, so there is no implication that could hold vacuously because of an impossible assumption.
The claim concerns ENNReal-valued lower integrals and asserts equality to the top element, meaning divergence to positive infinity rather than equality to a finite real integral.
The location and scale are fixed to 0 and 1; the statement does not quantify over general Cauchy parameters.
The integration domains and tail events use strict inequalities, although changing inclusion of the boundary points would not affect the intended Lebesgue integrals.
ambiguities: No substantive ambiguity is apparent: the target explicitly specifies the centered unit-scale Cauchy measure, both tail sets, both restricted Lebesgue integration domains, and equality to ENNReal infinity.
